messages:
Sam: quick callout  We9re seeing console N+1 actor lookups when a tenant opens the routing-policy list. Should we prefetch stubs or rely on on-demand hints?
Ryn: prefetching at page load helps UX but caused a spike last week. If we prefetch, do it under a tenant-scoped token bucket and randomized jitter.
Alexa: suggest a hybrid: optimistic prefetch for the first 5 visible cards only, then debounce background prefetch for the rest (250ms). That reduces tail burst.
Gabe: infra: need distinct quota buckets: `audit.stub_prefetch` (burstable) and `audit.stub_on_demand`. Also track prefetch_aborts when user navigates away.
Sam: UX: show placeholders and fill stubs as they arrive. If prefetch denied, fall back to a single-call hint when user clicks. Avoid blocking initial render.
Ryn: telemetry: instrument `audit.prefetch.attempt`, `audit.prefetch.success`, `audit.prefetch.denied_reason` and tag with `tenant_id_hash` + `route_group` so we can adjust bucket sizes per workload.
Alexa: caching: CDN-edge TTL 20s for stubs is reasonable. Add `Cache-Control: s-maxage=20, stale-while-revalidate=5`.
Gabe: security: ensure stubs contain no PII beyond display_name. Log only actor_id hashes for telemetry. Presign/download continues to require export entitlement check.
Sam: action items: Alexa implement prefetch with 5-card heuristic + 250ms debounce; Gabe add buckets + telemetry; Ryn add client jitter and abort signal; Sam will write console copy for masked states. Aim to roll to 5% canary Wed.
Devops-bot: Created ENG-8510: audit-stub-prefetch-quota (assignee: gabe).
